name: Constitutional Sideroblastic Anemia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Constitutional Sideroblastic Anemia

criteria.description: Presence of ringed sideroblasts in bone marrow aspirate
Microcytic, hypochromic anemia with ineffective erythropoiesis
Identification of pathogenic mutation in genes associated with sideroblastic anemia (e.g., ALAS2, SLC25A38)
Evidence of systemic iron overload without transfusion history
Positive family history consistent with inherited sideroblastic anemia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of ringed sideroblasts in bone marrow, microcytic hypochromic anemia, and identification of pathogenic mutation in sideroblastic anemia-associated genes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of acquired causes of sideroblastic anemia.

searchTerms: anemia with small, light-colored red cells

common.symptomName: Iron overload manifestations (e.g., elevated serum ferritin)

occasional.symptomName: Cardiac arrhythmias secondary to iron overload

occasional.symptomName: Bone deformities due to marrow expansion

abnormal bone shape from marrow growth

rare.symptomName: Neurological symptoms due to pyridoxine (vitamin B6) deficiency

neurological symptoms due to pyridoxine deficiency

rare.symptomName: Diabetes mellitus secondary to iron overload

heart muscle disease from iron buildup

laboratory: Presence of ringed sideroblasts on bone marrow iron stain
Elevated serum ferritin and transferrin saturation
imaging: MRI T2* showing iron overload in liver and heart
X-rays showing bone marrow expansion and deformities
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in ALAS2 gene (most common)
Mutations in SLC25A38, GLRX5, or other sideroblastic anemia-related genes
other: Family history consistent with X-linked or autosomal recessive inheritance
Response to pyridoxine therapy in some cases

distinguishingFeatures: History of toxin exposure or myelodysplastic syndrome
No ringed sideroblasts in bone marrow
Different genetic mutations affecting globin chains

redFlags: Progressive anemia refractory to standard treatment
Evidence of systemic iron overload without transfusion history
Development of cardiac or endocrine complications due to iron deposition
references: Cazzola M, et al. Sideroblastic Anemias. Hematology Am Soc Hematol Educ Program. 2017;2017(1): 1-9.
